plan.name: Compute faithful reader statecharts
plan.summary: Deliver the whole reader-statechart computation in one plumbing pull request: internal/statechart consumes the complete TLC graph, the lock and TLC-evaluated rule evidence, and evaluates a versioned, closed JSON view whose state(vars) and step(action, from, to) mappings only name states and transitions or request hiding. Include the TLC-backed invariant-evaluation adapter, total mapping and evidence validation, deterministic partitioning by reader label and violated invariant set, initial and concrete membership, and refusals with offending states, steps and view rules when hiding disconnects a chart state, removes its last outgoing arrow or hides only part of an arrow. Return deterministic chart data and a report with the lock's verbatim rule wording, trace-only temporal violations, actions unavailable to every member computed before hiding, all hidden steps and their multiplicities, source provenance and explicitly defined TLC and chart counts; handle every input through 500 reachable states, refuse larger graphs explicitly, and treat about 20 arrows as advice without truncation. Exercise the pure evaluator, complete graph accounting, all hiding refusals, isolation, replay and size boundaries offline, and wire a real pinned-TLC invariant-evaluation case into the existing integration suite while preserving the graph runner, its command and fake contracts, and existing dashboard behavior. Update SPEC.md with this ratified plan and supporting D-0016, D-0049, D-0105, D-0122 and D-0294 citations, the README's short link within its 400-line limit, and docs/statecharts.md with the delivered APIs, JSON view grammar, evidence boundary, refusals, counts, tests and current size limit; the new view and rule-evidence policy requires a decision recorded by the merger because this plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestReader586LifecycleAndCounts
tests.says: A lifecycle projection preserves every concrete state, initial membership and step occurrence, shows only concrete arrows, and reports exact hidden evidence, rule wording, provenance and separately defined counts.

tests.name: TestReader586HidingRefusals
tests.says: Hiding that disconnects a chart state, removes the last outgoing arrow or hides only some members of an arrow is refused with the offending states, steps and hiding rules.

tests.name: TestReader586UnavailableActions
tests.says: An action is unavailable only when no concrete member takes it and another reachable state does, using the graph before hiding and the original model action names.

tests.name: TestReader586RulesAndTemporalFacts
tests.says: Equal reader labels cannot merge different TLC invariant truth signatures, and temporal counterexamples stay intact as trace facts rather than invented state violations.

tests.name: TestReader586TotalityAndEvidenceRefusals
tests.says: Missing mappings, evaluation errors, incomplete rule evidence and inconsistent or unreachable graph data return a refusal and no partial chart.

tests.name: TestReader586DeterministicReplay
tests.says: Reordered graph input, repeated and concurrent evaluation produce identical serialized charts without mutating or retaining mutable caller data.

tests.name: TestReader586ClosedViewLanguage
tests.says: The JSON view is a bounded, typed, closed data language with no imports, I/O, execution or mutation; malformed and unsupported constructs are refused even in unreachable rules, and cancellation is preserved.

tests.name: TestReader586SizeAndArrowTarget
tests.says: All 500 reachable states and more than 20 arrows remain accounted for, 501 states produce an explicit size refusal, and the arrow target never drops evidence.

tests.name: TestReader586TLCRuleAdapter
tests.says: The adapter asks TLC to evaluate each locked invariant at every supplied concrete state, keeps the original graph and configuration intact, and requires complete boolean results joined by concrete identities.

tests.name: TestReader586TLCRuleAdapterRefusals
tests.says: Incomplete, malformed, mismatched or failed TLC evaluation and cancellation cannot supply invariant evidence, and temporary evaluator artifacts are cleaned up.

tests.name: TestReader586PinnedTLC
tests.says: An offline computation exercises the new API on every run; the opt-in pinned-TLC case evaluates two independent failing invariants and a structured value, and TestReader586RealIntegration runs that case in CI's existing integration suite.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and 11 acceptance tests covering the complete statechart computation, TLC rule evaluation, hiding validation, deterministic reports, and 500-state limit. The first check passed: every acceptance test fails on the base code, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
